books.section: Massachusetts and the New England Colonies
The Pilgrims and the Massachusetts Bay Company

options.misconception: Treats two different English colonies as the same kind of venture.
options.text: Both colonies were founded by the same company for the same purpose, seeking profit and a godly community together in America.

options.misconception: Reverses the mortality — Jamestown lost most of its people, while Massachusetts Bay grew.
options.text: Both colonies lost most of their settlers in their first winters on the coast and nearly failed entirely.

options.misconception: Reads a large migration as a small one.
options.text: Massachusetts Bay was settled by only a handful of families from England seeking profit and trade.
Jamestown began as a company venture of men seeking profit and nearly died, while Massachusetts Bay brought families seeking a godly community.

rationales.A: Jamestown was a Virginia Company venture seeking profit, while Massachusetts Bay was settled by Puritans building a godly community; the companies and purposes differed.
rationales.B: Jamestown lost nearly 90 percent of its people in the starving time, but Massachusetts Bay grew, drawing more than 20,000 settlers in twelve years.
rationales.C: Massachusetts Bay drew more than 20,000 settlers, whole families of middling sorts, not a handful of families.
rationales.D: Jamestown's 144 men nearly vanished in its first years, while Massachusetts Bay's family migration of more than 20,000 made it a lasting settlement.
rationales.general:
1. Compare the two English rows. Jamestown starts with 144 men and nearly vanishes; Massachusetts Bay brings more than 20,000 people in twelve years.
2. Ask who came in each case. Background: Jamestown's settlers were mostly men seeking profit, while Massachusetts Bay brought whole families of farmers and craftsmen.
3. Ask why they came. Profit drove the Virginia Company; a godly community drove the Puritans.
4. Name the contrast. One English colony was a fragile company venture; the other was a family migration that took root and grew.
Remember: when two colonies share a flag, ask who came and why, and the differences usually explain which one survived.

stimulus.source_note: Table built from figures given in the three books; France's count is given qualitatively because the books give no exact number.
stimulus.text:
Early Atlantic crossings, 1607-1650

| Group | People | When |
|---|---|---|
| Spaniards to the New World | About 350,000 | By 1650 |
| English settlers at Jamestown | 144 landed; only 38 still alive a year later | 1607-1608 |
| English settlers at Jamestown | About 500 in the colony; nearly 90% died in the 'starving time' | Winter 1609-1610 |
| English settlers to Massachusetts Bay | More than 20,000 | 1630-1642 |
| French settlers to New France | Few, mostly single men; the books give no exact count | 1600s |
